title: Answer the repeated read from memory
impact: Moonshot: rejected, and the reason is not the one the numbers suggest. Exps 265 and 269 established that the isolate round trip is most of a hot point read and that running the query on the caller cannot be made safe; a cache hit runs no SQLite at all, so it collects the same headroom without the bounding problem exp 269 died on. It works: a hit costs 0.48 us against a 4.65 us dispatch, reproduced at -90.0%/-90.1% on a repeated point read, -92.1%/-91.9% at 21 columns, -90.2%/-89.6% across eight cycled parameter sets and -95.1%/-95.7% on a 20-row page, with peak RSS flat or lower. Every adversarial guard is neutral, and two of them wrote the design: describing a statement on first sight rather than second cost a reproduced +21% on a never-repeating SQL workload, and a table-to-queries invalidation index cost +16-19% on a read/write-alternating lane before per-table version stamps moved the cost off the writer entirely. What kills it is scope, not bookkeeping. resqlite's invalidation is built from its own preupdate hook, so it hears only writes made through the same `Database`; a probe that commits through a second connection to the same file gets the pre-write value back from `select()` while a fresh connection sees the new one. `stream()` has always had that boundary and documents it, `select()` has not, and the failure is silent. `PRAGMA data_version` would close it and was measured rather than assumed — 2 us p50 idle, 1 us p50 under a committing foreign writer, 10 us max — which makes a validated hit ~2 us against 4.65 us, about 2x instead of 10x, bought by putting a SQLite connection on the calling isolate, which is exp 269's rejected architecture. Incidence was measured too: 17.7% of Chat Sim's 9,006 reads would hit against 84.3% of Feed Paging's 140, a near-5x spread that makes the value workload-shaped rather than constant. The release suite cannot judge this at all — its read lanes repeat one statement with nothing writing, so `Select -> Maps` at 100 rows reads 0.040 -> 0.005 ms and that number is the benchmark measuring itself. Runtime reverted; the focused harness, the foreign-writer probe, the incidence probe and the `data_version` price are kept, and the successor named is the narrow one: serve `select()` from an active stream's own last result, where the caller has already accepted stream semantics.
